To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
people rely on thoughts more to form their evaluations when the thoughts come from the self rather than an external source.

people rely more on their thoughts to form attitudes when they perceive their thoughts to originate from the self than when they are induced to believe that their thoughts come from an external source.
people are more likely to rely on their thoughts when they are perceived to originate from the self than when they are perceived as originating from external sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the perceived origin of thoughts in attitude formation and maintenance.
how people perceive the origin of their thoughts and how this influences their attitudes.
the impact of the origin of thoughts on the reliance on those thoughts in the formation of attitudes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
when people perceive their thoughts to come from the self versus other origins they will rely more on their thoughts in the attitude formation process.
people rely more on their thoughts when they believe their thoughts originate from the self than when they believe their source is an external one.

the perceived origins of thoughts impact the extent to which individuals rely on them to form their attitudes, with the impact of origin being greater when thoughts come from the self than when they come from external sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people’s attitudes are more strongly influenced by their own thoughts when those thoughts are perceived as coming from the self.
when we perceive thoughts to be from the self, we rely on them more to make judgments.
people rely more on their thoughts when they perceive them to originate from their self than from an external source.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when we believe our thoughts come from the self, we are more likely to rely on them when forming attitudes.
when people believe their thoughts are their own, they are more likely to rely on them to form attitudes.
when people think their thoughts originate from the self, they rely on them more in attitude judgments, even when the thoughts are negative.
